title: Kareena Kapoor Khan Gets Legal Notice Over Quranic Verse Pendant Worn for Diwali
excerpt: Reports say Abbas Hafeez sent a legal notice to Kareena Kapoor Khan and stylist Rhea Kapoor asking for Diwali photographs showing an emerald pendant inscribed with Ayat-ul-Kursi to be removed and for an apology — a demand, not a court finding.
body:
• Actor Kareena Kapoor Khan and stylist Rhea Kapoor have been served a legal notice over a Diwali look featuring a 30-carat emerald pendant described as inscribed with Ayat-ul-Kursi, a Quranic verse.
  • The notice was sent by Bhopal-based political leader Abbas Hafeez, who, as reported, asked for the photographs to be removed and for a public apology — a legal notice is a demand, not a finding.
  • The pendant was described by Rhea Kapoor in her Instagram post as a Bhopal royal family heirloom; that provenance is as described by the stylist, not independently verified in the reports read.
  • As of November 12, 2026, neither Kapoor Khan nor Rhea Kapoor had issued a response, according to the reports read.

Bollywood actor Kareena Kapoor Khan and celebrity stylist Rhea Kapoor have been served a legal notice over Kapoor Khan's Diwali look, in which she wore a pendant identified as a historic heirloom of the erstwhile Bhopal royal family, inscribed with a Quranic verse. The reports were published by The Hollywood Reporter India and Bollywood Hungama on November 12, 2026. The dispute is about presentation of the pendant in social media photographs, as described by the notice sender.

What happened

The pendant in question is a 30-carat emerald piece whose religious inscription has become the focal point of the objection, The Hollywood Reporter India reported. The verse inscribed on it is Ayat-ul-Kursi, the 255th verse of the second chapter of the Quran, Surah Al-Baqarah, both reports said.

Kapoor Khan's ensemble comprised a beige kaftan paired with a matching turban, which carried a kalgi, The Hollywood Reporter India reported. Bollywood Hungama described the outfit as a silver kaftan paired with a matching turban and the emerald pendant. Rhea Kapoor shared details of the look on social media.

“Real movie star, real chandi, real heirlooms and real personal style. Kareena in a pure chandi kaftan and turban by @punit.balana, wearing a 200-year-old kalgi from the Nawab of Bhopal and the Begum of Bhopal’s 30-carat emerald, carved with the Ayat-ul-Kursi,” Rhea Kapoor wrote, as quoted by both reports.

Both reports link the emerald to the Begums of Bhopal and to Saif Ali Khan's family, quoting Rhea Kapoor noting that Saif's grandmother, Sajida Sultan, was the daughter of the last ruling Nawab of Bhopal. Those provenance details come from the stylist's post; they are not presented here as independently authenticated.

Who issued what — only as sourced

The notice was sent by Abbas Hafeez, a Bhopal-based political leader, The Hollywood Reporter India reported. Bollywood Hungama identified him as a Congress spokesperson. The Hollywood Reporter India said he asked Khan and Kapoor to publicly apologise to the Muslim community, and that Rhea Kapoor was included in the notice in her capacity as the stylist who put together the look and described the pendant publicly as a Bhopal royal heirloom.

Bollywood Hungama reported that the notice seeks the removal of the actress's photographs from social media and a public apology. It reported that Hafeez objected to the use of the Quranic verse as part of a fashion accessory, and that, according to him, the pendant represents the Islamic heritage of the Begums of Bhopal and was commissioned as an expression of religious faith rather than for fashion purposes.

“Let me make it very clear: people are free to celebrate whichever festival they wish and wear whatever clothes they want. Our objection is only to the Quranic verse. Even if she had worn it on Eid, it would still have been objectionable,” Hafeez said, as quoted by Bollywood Hungama from FPJ.

Bollywood Hungama also reported that advocate Mohammad Zafar explained that the legal notice demands the removal of Kapoor Khan's social media photographs, and stated that if the request is not addressed, further legal remedies could be considered.

A legal notice is a demand sent by one party to another. It is an allegation and a claim by the sender, not a court case, a judicial ruling or a finding that any law was broken. No court finding is reported in either source read for this article.

Responses, only as sourced

Bollywood Hungama reported that the Hindu Utsav Samiti has come out in support of Kareena Kapoor Khan. It did not, in the text read, quote a specific statement from the group beyond that support.

As of November 12, Kapoor Khan has not issued a public response to the notice, and her representatives have also not issued a statement, The Hollywood Reporter India reported. That is the position as reported on November 12; silence should not be read as acceptance or rejection of the demands.

Kapoor Khan also shared pictures of her outfit, writing, “Diwali is all about traditions done right”, The Hollywood Reporter India reported — a post about the look, not presented as a response to the notice.
